newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Gazprom sags, other shares cautiously up.
newsitem.headline: Russia Gazprom sags, other shares cautiously up.

text.p: Russian natural gas producer Gazprom continued its downward slide in late afternoon trading on Thursday, but some traders saw other leading shares, which were sidling up by the end of the day, ticking higher on Friday.
"I would say 60-40 that the market will rise tomorrow, especially if the Dow Jones rises," said Prospekt's head of overseas trading Igor Lossavio.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index rose to 352.64 at 1200 GMT, after closing on Wednesday at 351.40.

National electricity company UES edged up to $0.3110 at 1355 GMT from Wednesday's closing $0.3104 and regional utility Irkutskenergo nosed higher to $0.272 from $0.268 on the markets highest turnover of $11.9 million.
Traders were unable to say what the demand in Irkutskenergo was due to.
Oil producer Tatneft which had one of the highest turnovers on the market, traded at $83.00, down from Wednesday's closing $83.10 and off a high of $84.50.

Tatneft announced on Thursday dividends on ordinary shares with a face value of 10,000 roubles would rise to 6,000 roubles from 5,000 roubles paid in 1995. Dividends on preferred shares would rise to 10,000 roubles from 6,000 roubles.

But Rye Man and Gor trader Igor Kozhechkin said the market was little changed, saying investors burned by Wednesday's decree on share ownership in natural gas producer Gazprom, which was trading at $0.6030, down from $0.6495, were still cautious.
"Most volume today was in Gazprom and Irkutskenergo," Kozhechkin said. "Otherwise the market was very quiet."
